The Book of the Righteous Wirāz is the Zoroastrian journey through heaven and hell, often called the Persian Divine Comedy. It was written in Middle Persian (Pahlavi) and took its present form in the ninth or tenth century, from older material. This first chapter sets the scene. Alexander has burned the scriptures and killed the priests, the faith has broken into sects and doubt, and the priests gather at the Farnbāg Fire to send one of their number to the other world to learn whether their rites reach the gods at all. Seven men are picked, then three, then one, Wirāz, who asks only that the choice be confirmed by lot. In the chapters that follow he drinks wine and mang, his soul leaves his body for seven days, and he is shown the rewards of the blessed and the punishments of the damned.
